sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 is a sheet of Garfield, not Rutherford: its header reads Garfield, N.J., and it is bound in this Rutherford record with a Rutherford stamp. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north a little to the right of straight up, and covers the business centre of Garfield along the Erie Railroad's Bergen County Branch, from Commerce Street at the top to Passaic Street at the bottom and from Palisade Avenue on the left to Marsellus Place on the right. The railroad runs down the middle of the sheet with a passenger station at Passaic Street. West of the tracks are dwellings and stores on Hudson, Hepworth Place and Somerset, the First Presbyterian Church on Commerce, Garfield School No. 6 on Palisade Avenue, the Somerset Hotel, a bake shop and the works of the Standard Match Co. on Hepworth Place, with splint, packing, paper cutting and drying rooms. Between the tracks and Pierre Avenue lies the yard of the Gerritsen & Stewart Lumber Co., with lumber sheds, a planing mill and builders' supplies. East of the tracks, along Midland Avenue, Harrison Avenue and Marsellus Place, are the police and fire department building of Fire Co. No. 1, a bank, Holy Innocents Episcopal Church, Holy Name R.C. Church, a small triangular park and more dwellings. Water pipes and hydrants are marked in every street, and block numbers 23 to 49 are shown; sheets 8, 10, 11 and 13 adjoin.
notes: Pierre Avenue is modern Atlantic Avenue.
Bogart Avenue south of Passaic is on the line of modern Midland Avenue; the modern Midland Avenue / Passaic Street junction falls on the drawn Bogart Avenue corner.
Sheet header reads Garfield, N.J.; the sheet is part of the Garfield volume, not a Rutherford street sheet.
Drawn at 50 ft to an inch, unlike the Rutherford sheets at 100 ft.

Garfield, not Rutherford (printed 'Garfield N.J.', stamped Rutherford): Commerce St to Passaic St, Palisade Av to Marsellus Pl, Erie RR Bergen County Branch; Standard Match Co, Gerritsen & Stewart Lumber. 50 ft to an inch. One part.

sheet-29-1.description: The main part of sheet 29 covers the northwest corner of Rutherford along the Passaic River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Riverside Avenue follows the river bank across the top of the part, and the river itself fills the upper area. Rutherford Avenue, the line between the borough and the Township of Union, runs down the left edge, and Pierrepont Avenue down the right edge. Between them the ground is laid out on curving streets: Stuyvesant Avenue and Edgewood Place sweep across the middle, West Gouverneur Avenue runs straight down the centre, Preble Place is marked as not opened, and Park Avenue crosses the lower half diagonally to meet East Gouverneur Avenue, Woodland Avenue and Vanness Avenue near the bottom, with College Place a short street off Rutherford Avenue. Much of the area is still divided into large or empty lots, with scattered detached frame dwellings, many of them newly built, and denser rows of houses along Park Avenue and Edgewood Place. Named premises are few: the coal and ice yard of J. P. Jorralemon on Riverside Avenue and the First Presbyterian Church of Lyndhurst at the corner of Rutherford Avenue and Park Avenue. Water pipes are marked in most streets, a fire alarm box stands at Park Avenue and West Gouverneur Avenue, and block numbers 9 to 27 and 101 to 103 are shown. Sheets 30 and 37 adjoin, and an inset of the river front at Woodward Avenue occupies the upper left corner (part 2).
notes: Pierrepont Avenue is modern West Pierrepont Avenue; Vanness Avenue is modern East Van Ness Avenue.
Preble Place is marked not opened.
Rutherford Avenue is drawn as the borough line with the Township of Union (now Lyndhurst).
Modern College Place does not follow the drawn College Place and was not used; Marginal Road (a modern highway ramp) crosses the left side of the part.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Riverside Av to Park Av, Rutherford Av to Pierrepont Av; Stuyvesant Av, Edgewood Pl, W. Gouverneur Av) and 2 inset at top left (Riverside Av, Woodward Av, W. Newell Av along the Passaic River: West Rutherford Color & Chemical Co, Rutherford Cement Construction Co).

sheet-29-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 29 is an inset in the upper left corner, separated from the main map by a heavy line and drawn at the same scale of 100 feet to an inch and the same orientation. It shows a short stretch of Riverside Avenue along the Passaic River in Rutherford, between West Newell Avenue and Woodward Avenue, which lies about 700 metres northeast of the main part along the same river front. Between the avenue and the river stand the works of the West Rutherford Color & Chemical Co., makers of dye stuffs, with a laboratory, dye manufacturing and storage and drying buildings beside a wooden trestle and hoisting engine; the coal shed of the Hasselhuhn Williams Co.; and the stone and wagon sheds and a tool house on piles belonging to the Borough of Rutherford. South of Riverside Avenue the block between West Newell Avenue and Woodward Avenue holds the block-making shed and cement storage of the Rutherford Cement Construction Co. A dwelling stands east of Woodward Avenue. The lettered points A and B along the dividing line, and the number 30, match this corner to the adjoining sheet 30.
notes: Placed from two junctions only (helmert): Riverside Avenue at Woodward Avenue and at West Newell Avenue. Low confidence.
Riverside Avenue is drawn much wider here than its labelled width.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Riverside Av to Park Av, Rutherford Av to Pierrepont Av; Stuyvesant Av, Edgewood Pl, W. Gouverneur Av) and 2 inset at top left (Riverside Av, Woodward Av, W. Newell Av along the Passaic River: West Rutherford Color & Chemical Co, Rutherford Cement Construction Co).

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 covers the northwest part of the Borough of Rutherford, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Riverside Avenue and the Passaic River cut across the upper left corner, where a compass rose is printed. Carmita Avenue crosses the upper third of the sheet and Montross Avenue the middle; Mortimer Avenue closes the sheet at the bottom. Pierrepont Avenue runs down the left edge, and Vreeland Avenue slants across the left half. The parallel avenues to the right are West Newell Avenue, Woodward Avenue, Donaldson Avenue and West Passaic Avenue. Much of the upper and left part is open, with large blocks (numbers 13 and 14) cut into narrow lots or not yet divided, and a street marked not opened runs east and west across the upper left. Stuyvesant Avenue and Edgewood Place enter at the left edge. Houses are concentrated south of Montross Avenue and along the avenues on the right, almost all detached frame dwellings, many with garages and outbuildings; Riverview Avenue is a short street at the lower left lined with houses on both sides. The Lincoln School stands on Montross Avenue near Pierrepont Avenue, the Rutherford Tennis Club has grounds beside Woodward Avenue, and a florist's greenhouse range stands on Woodward Avenue. At the top of the sheet the Garraways Co., photographic printing, occupies a brick building on Carmita Avenue, with its works listed as heat by steam, electric light and power, and the sheet notes copying and printing and manufacturing of photographs. Water pipes are marked in the streets, and block numbers run from 2 to 34. Sheets 29, 31, 37, 38 and 39 adjoin.
notes: Pierrepont Avenue is modern West Pierrepont Avenue.
Vreeland Avenue is on the modern Vreeland Avenue line.
A street running east and west across the upper left is marked not opened; it carries no printed name.
The Lincoln School and florist names were not read with confidence.
100 ft. NW Rutherford, Carmita Av to Mortimer Av, Pierrepont Av to W. Passaic Av; Lincoln School, Garraways Co. One part.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 covers the west side of the Borough of Rutherford north of Montross Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. West Passaic Avenue runs down the left edge and Union Avenue down the right edge. A wide diagonal road, Jackson Avenue, enters at the left and runs across the top of the sheet, crossing Insley Avenue, Raymond Avenue, Hastings Avenue and Clark Avenue. Below it the blocks are laid out regularly: Belford Avenue, Springfield Avenue, Santiago Avenue and Carmita Avenue cross the sheet, with Cooper Place and Francisco Avenue running between them. The lower third has Hollister Avenue, Fairview Avenue and Alwyn Terrace, and Prospect Place with a Proposed street beside it, down to Montross Avenue at the bottom. The area is almost entirely detached frame dwellings, many with garages, built most densely along Santiago Avenue, Springfield Avenue and Carmita Avenue, while the upper left, around blocks 177 to 179, is largely open lots, and the lower left blocks are lightly built. The Union Public School stands on Springfield Avenue near Union Avenue, and next to it the fire department house of the West End Engine and Hose Company No. 3, with a bakery. Raymond Avenue, Wells Place and Beech Street end at the right edge. A compass rose is printed near the lower right corner. Water pipes of 6 inches are marked along most streets, fire hydrants and a fire alarm box stand at street corners, and block numbers run from 18 to 182. Sheets 30, 32, 38 and 39 adjoin.
notes: Jackson Avenue is drawn as a wide diagonal road at the upper left; its junction with West Passaic Avenue sat 4.8 m off the fit and was left out.
Belford Avenue is printed 'Belford Av.' and is Belford Avenue in modern data.
The adjoining sheets named in the description were read from the margins; the sheet header reads Garfield, N.J.
100 ft. Rutherford west side, Jackson Av (diagonal) to Montross Av, W. Passaic Av to Union Av; Union Public School. One part. Jackson Av / W. Passaic Av excluded (4.8 m).

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 covers the central west side of the Borough of Rutherford, between Union Avenue on the left and the Erie Railroad's Rutherford and East Rutherford boundary on the right, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Jackson Avenue crosses the top left, with Morrisse Place, marked not opened, above Raymond Avenue. Down the sheet run Union Avenue, Washington Avenue, Sunderland Avenue, Saint Clair Avenue and Morse Avenue, with Erie Avenue along the railroad at the right. Crossing them from top to bottom are Wells Place, Hawthorne, Beech, Myrtle, Walnut, Carmita Avenue, Courrier, Prospect Place, Hasbrouck Place and Montross Avenue. The blocks are numbered 86 to 100 and 170 to 175. Nearly all the buildings are detached frame dwellings with auto garages; the densest rows are in the middle of the sheet between Washington Avenue and Erie Avenue, while the upper left and the large block 92 are mostly divided into empty narrow lots. Stores, a small plant and a church group stand near the corner of Union Avenue and Beech. A fire alarm box stands on Morse Avenue at Courrier. At the right edge the railroad right of way is marked with the boundary line of Rutherford and East Rutherford, a stream and pond near the upper right are shown in blue, and a compass rose is printed beside them. A concrete bridge is marked at the bottom right, and the margin names Poplar Street and Oak Street on the adjoining sheet 33. Six-inch water pipes are marked along nearly every street. Sheets 31, 33, 38 and 40 adjoin.
notes: Erie Avenue is modern West Erie Avenue; Hawthorne, Beech, Myrtle and Walnut are Hawthorne Street, Beech Street, Myrtle Street and Walnut Street; Courrier is Courrier Place; Saint Clair Avenue is printed St. Clair Av..
Morrisse Place is marked not opened and does not appear in the modern data.
The street names read from the overview (Sunderland, Wells Place, Erie Avenue) are medium confidence on exact spelling; 'Poplar St.' and 'Oak St.' are partly cut at the right edge.
Sheet header reads Garfield, N.J.
100 ft. Union Av to the Erie RR (East Rutherford line), Jackson Av to Montross Av. One part.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 covers the west side of the Borough of Rutherford south of the Passaic River district, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Rutherford Avenue runs down the left edge as the line between the borough and the Township of Union, and Pierrepont Avenue runs down the right edge. The left half of the sheet is a series of long parallel blocks laid out from Delafield Avenue at the top through Lafayette Avenue, Daniels Avenue, Wheaton Place, Lincoln Avenue and Wilson Avenue to Ridge Road, almost all of them cut into narrow empty lots, with Lafayette Avenue and Wheaton Place marked not opened and a ball grounds shown in the large block 102A beside a compass rose. Woodland Avenue and Van Ness Avenue cross the sheet from top to bottom and Van Riper Avenue and 8th Avenue run down the lower left, with Sylvan and Summit Avenue cutting across at the bottom. Houses are few on the left side and concentrated in the right-hand blocks, around Wheaton Place, Lincoln Avenue and Wilson Avenue, and along Pierrepont Avenue and Ridge Road, where detached frame dwellings with garages stand on regular lots. The Pierrepont School, a brick building of two stories, stands at the corner of Pierrepont Avenue and Lincoln Avenue. Block numbers run from 102 to 131 with several lettered subdivisions, and 6-inch water pipes are marked in most streets. Park is lettered at the top right corner. Sheets 29, 38 and 47 adjoin, and the sheet header reads Garfield, N.J.
notes: Daniels Avenue is modern Daniel Avenue; Van Ness Avenue is East Van Ness Avenue; Pierrepont Avenue is East Pierrepont Avenue; Sylvan is Sylvan Street; 8th Avenue was not matched to a modern street and was not used as control.
Lafayette Avenue and Wheaton Place are marked not opened on the sheet.
Modern Woodland Avenue has twin nodes about 12 m apart at Lincoln, Daniel and Wheaton; both were accepted for one drawn junction.
The Pierrepont School and Park at the top right were read from the overview only (medium confidence).
100 ft. Delafield Av to Summit Av, Rutherford Av (Union Township line) to Pierrepont Av. One part. Printed 8th Av not matched to a modern street.

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 covers the centre of the Borough of Rutherford north of the Erie Main Line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It runs from Mortimer Avenue along the top to Orient Way at the bottom, and from Pierrepont Avenue on the left to West and East Passaic Avenue on the right. Park Avenue, the borough's main street, crosses the upper half diagonally from Riverview Avenue to the junction of the Passaic avenues, and Lincoln Avenue, Ridge Road, Sylvan Street and Mountain Way cross the lower half as parallel streets, with the Newell avenues, the Park places, Summit Cross and Highland Cross running between them. The area is almost entirely detached frame dwellings on regular lots, many with automobile garages behind. The commercial and civic buildings stand along Park Avenue: a block at the corner of Park Avenue and East Park Place holds the Masonic Hall, the fire department house of the volunteer chemical and hose company, and the storage, carpet cleaning and upholstering premises of Geo. B. Holman & Co., built of reinforced concrete. Across Park Avenue lie Lincoln Park, a triangle at the meeting of Park Avenue and the Passaic avenues, the Park School and the Rutherford Baptist Church. The Sylvan School stands on Sylvan Street near Highland Cross, and an apartment building called The Whittier faces Park Avenue. Water pipes are marked along most streets. Block numbers run from 55 to 144, and the adjoining sheets 30, 37, 39, 41 and 48 are named around the margins.
notes: Park Avenue was left out of the control: its junctions sat 3 to 5 m off the fit to the other streets.
The sheet header reads Garfield, N.J., the volume this Rutherford sheet belongs to.

100 ft. Park Av, Mortimer Av to Orient Way, Pierrepont Av to E./W. Passaic Av; Lincoln Park, Park School, Sylvan School. One part. Park Avenue left out (its junctions 3 to 5 m off the rest of the fit).

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39 covers a section of the Borough of Rutherford between Montross Avenue at the top and Chestnut at the bottom, from West Passaic Avenue on the left to Union Avenue on the right, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Fairview Avenue runs down from Montross Avenue to Wood, and Elliott Place and Elliott Terrace, Milton Court and Irving Place lie in the left-hand blocks, with Mortimer Avenue below them, Home Avenue near the bottom, and Franklin Place and Ames Avenue running down to Chestnut. Hackett Place, Maple Street and Grove Street enter at the right edge. The built-up ground is in the left strip, along Home Avenue and Chestnut, and in the upper right; the centre of the sheet, blocks 48, 49 and 62 to 65, is open land with only the lines of proposed streets. Named premises are Elliott Manor, the large estate house with a swimming pool owned by S. M. Schatzkin in block 35A, Grace Episcopal Church on Elliott Terrace, a Methodist church on West Passaic Avenue, and, near the bottom, St. Mary's R.C. Church with St. Mary's School on Home Avenue at Ames Avenue. A few dwellings stand in the open centre near the Union Avenue edge and a compass rose is printed in the middle right. Dwellings are mostly detached two-story frame houses, with garages in the rear. Fire alarm boxes stand at several corners and 6-inch water pipes run in the streets. Block numbers run from 35 to 70. Sheets 30, 31, 38, 40, 41 and 42 adjoin, and the header reads Garfield, N.J.
notes: Wood is Wood Street; Chestnut is Chestnut Street; Elliott Terrace and Elliott Place both lie on modern Elliott Place; Fairview Avenue and Franklin Place meet on the same modern line (Fairview Avenue).
The Methodist church name on West Passaic Avenue and the Hollister Avenue lettering at the top were read from the overview only (medium confidence).
100 ft. Montross Av to Chestnut, W. Passaic Av to Union Av; open centre; Elliott Manor, St. Mary's R.C. Church. One part.

sheet-40.description: Sheet 40 covers the Rutherford and East Rutherford border district on both sides of the Erie Railroad's main line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. The multi-track railroad crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the upper right and is also the boundary between the two boroughs, with Railroad Avenue running beside the tracks on each side. West of the tracks, in Rutherford, are Montross Avenue at the top, Beckwith Place, Morse Avenue, Sidney Avenue, Hackett Place, Wood, Elm, Grove, Maple, Ivy Place, Ayer Place and Chestnut, with Union Avenue at the left edge, Washington Avenue and Erie Avenue running between them. East of the tracks, in East Rutherford, are Herman, Mozart, Clinton Place, Humboldt and Uhland, crossed by Main and Grove, with Everett Place at the bottom. The Washington Public School stands on Wood near Union Avenue. In East Rutherford the industrial buildings cluster along Mozart and Clinton Place: the Banner Utility Co., makers of brushes, a handkerchief embroidering works with machines, the American Syringe Mfg. Co., the fire department house of East Rutherford Hose Co. No. 1 and the Borough Department of Public Works, and Public School No. 1 on Humboldt. A long pink factory building stands beside the tracks on Railroad Avenue near the bottom. Dwellings are mostly detached frame houses with garages; the middle left blocks near the tracks, 53 and 54, are open. A compass rose and the block numbers 40 to 72 are printed, along with 6-inch water pipes in the streets. Sheets 32, 35, 39, 43 and 44 adjoin, and the header reads Rutherford and E. Rutherford.
notes: Erie Avenue is modern West Erie Avenue; Wood, Elm, Grove, Maple, Chestnut, Herman, Mozart, Humboldt, Uhland and Main are the modern Street names; Clinton Place is not in the modern data.
Two modern Maple Street / Union Avenue nodes lie about 20 m apart; the junction was accepted once.
Erie Avenue / Montross Avenue and Ayer Place / Union Avenue junctions sat 4 m from the fit and are medium confidence.
Names on the lower margin of the sheet (Everett Place) and the Grove Street across the tracks were read from the overview only.
100 ft. Rutherford and East Rutherford on both sides of the Erie Main Line, Hackett Pl to Uhland. One part.

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 shows the business centre of Rutherford west of the Erie Railroad station, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, twice the scale of most sheets of the volume, with north toward the upper right. Park Avenue, the main street, crosses the sheet from the upper left to the lower right and is lined along its north side with stores, a public library, the Union Club, a laundry, a confectioner, a tailor and a delicatessen, a market, a cloak factory and the boarding house called The Maples, many of them built of brick or concrete. Chestnut runs along the top edge, Ridge Road across the upper middle, and Sylvan across the middle, with East Passaic Avenue down the left side and The Terrace, a curved street, in the lower half; Franklin Place and Kip Avenue lie at the upper right, and Spring Dell and Ettrick Terrace (The Sweep) at the lower right. The First Presbyterian Church, with a slated spire above a stone tower, stands in block 119 inside the triangle of Park Avenue and Ridge Road, and the Borough Hall with its auditorium and the Post Office stand on the north side of Park Avenue near Franklin Place, and block 126, between Ridge Road and Sylvan, is a row of detached dwellings with garages. Blocks 127 and 128 are wedges of stores along Park Avenue. At the lower right the C. R. Soley Co., makers of sashes and mouldings, has a lumber storage building, sheds and an office, and several dwellings stand in the blocks around The Terrace. The 6-inch and 12-inch water pipes are marked, hydrants and fire alarm boxes stand at the corners, and block numbers run from 73 to 146. Sheets 38, 39, 42, 43 and 48 adjoin; the header reads Garfield, N.J. and Rutherford.
notes: Drawn at 50 ft to an inch; the fitted rotation (about 62 degrees) differs from the 53 degrees of the 100 ft sheets.
Chestnut is Chestnut Street; Sylvan is Sylvan Street; Ettrick Terrace is also lettered The Sweep.
Lincoln Avenue and Mountain Way at the left edge, and the Library and Union Club names, were read from the overview only (medium confidence).
50 ft. Park Av business district, Chestnut to Sylvan, E. Passaic Av to Spring Dell; The Terrace, C. R. Soley Co. One part.

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42 shows the heart of Rutherford's business district and the Erie Railroad station, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Park Avenue crosses the sheet from the upper left to the middle right, lined with brick stores and offices on its north side: the Rutherford National Bank, a Public Service Corporation office, a cigar manufacturer, bakeries, markets, plumbers, a jeweller and a Wells Fargo Express office. The avenue ends at Station Square near the station, at the lower right, where the Erie Railroad's tracks and the passenger station and its platform shed are drawn. Chestnut runs along the top and Kip Avenue below it, with Franklin Place on the left, Ames Avenue and Union Avenue down the middle and right, and Erie Avenue along the tracks at the right edge. North of Park Avenue, between Ames Avenue and Union Avenue, stand the Elks Home, the fire department house, the Criterion Theatre (moving pictures), garages with capacities of 16, 18 and 30 cars, a bakery, bowling alleys and the office of the Rutherford Water Co. West of Park Avenue are blocks of dwellings between Chestnut and Kip Avenue, and the Hushag Steam Laundry, Wm. Black & Co. roofing material and a bottling works behind the stores. South of Park Avenue lie Glen Road, Sylvan, Spring Dell and Orient Way, with auto repair shops, a stable, an express office and the Rutherford Steam Laundry in blocks 147 and 148. Block numbers 74 to 76, 147 and 148 are shown with 6-inch and 12-inch water pipes. Sheets 39, 41, 43 and 48 adjoin and the header reads Rutherford.
notes: Drawn at 50 ft to an inch.
Chestnut is Chestnut Street; Sylvan is Sylvan Street; Erie Avenue is modern West Erie Avenue; Station Square is Station Square in modern data.
Orient Way and Glen Road junctions sat 4 m off the fit and are medium confidence; Orient Way's modern right of way is wider than drawn.
The name 'Roney Place' at the upper right edge is partly cut off (medium confidence), as are the company names Hushag and Wells Fargo.
50 ft. Park Av and the Erie station, Chestnut to Orient Way, Franklin Pl to Union Av and Station Square. One part.

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, twice the scale of most Rutherford sheets, with north toward the upper right. It covers the ground on both sides of the Erie Railroad's main line at the Rutherford station, where the borough line between Rutherford and East Rutherford follows the tracks diagonally across the sheet. On the Rutherford side, between Union Avenue and Erie Avenue, are dwellings on Chestnut and Agnew Place, a plaster ornament works and a private concrete-block building on Agnew Place, two concrete garages, a machine shop, a livery stable and a vulcanizing shop, with buried gasoline tanks marked. On the East Rutherford side Railroad Avenue runs beside the tracks; between it and Orchard lie the lumber yard of J. P. Cooper & Co., with lumber sheds, piled lumber, paper and shingle storage and an office, a bank office, a hay and grain store and the printing plant of the Chemical Bank Note Co. Farther east are dwellings along Everett Place and Boiling Springs Avenue. Across Park Avenue at the bottom, between Union Avenue and Orchard, stand a row of stores, The Park House hotel with a beer garden and pool room, more dwellings, and largely open lots reaching to Van Winkle. Water pipes up to 12 inches are marked in the streets. Block numbers 22 and 68 to 73 are shown, and sheets 40, 42, 44, 45 and 48 adjoin.
notes: Erie Avenue is modern West Erie Avenue; Orchard is Orchard Street; Van Winkle is Van Winkle Street.
Drawn at 50 ft to an inch.
The Park Avenue / Union Avenue junction was left out (4.7 m off the fit; complex modern junction with West Erie Avenue).

50 ft to an inch. Rutherford and East Rutherford at the Erie station: Chestnut St to Van Winkle, Union Av to beyond Orchard; Erie Av (modern West Erie Avenue) and Railroad Av on either side of the Erie Main Line; J. P. Cooper & Co. lumber yard, Chemical Bank Note Co. One part.

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47 covers the southwest corner of the Borough of Rutherford, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Rutherford Avenue runs down the left edge, marking the line with the Township of Union (now Lyndhurst), and Pierrepont Avenue is lettered at the right edge. The upper left has the short blocks of Summit Avenue, 8th Avenue and Van Riper Avenue, with Mountain Way, Orient Way and Feronia Way crossing as long parallel streets and Woodland Avenue, Crane Avenue, Nevins and William running between them. The streets are laid out in large blocks (numbered 132 to 164) that are mostly empty lots divided by property lines, with a scatter of detached frame dwellings, a few outbuildings and garages concentrated along Orient Way, Woodland Avenue and the right-hand blocks near Pierrepont Avenue. Nevins is marked not opened. Below Feronia Way the sheet is largely open ground: a short street named Spring, a compass rose, and the long diagonal strips of Ely Craft Parkway and Meadow Road running across the lower half, with only two or three small buildings beside Meadow Road. Meadow Road is a wide road at the bottom, and the sheet ends with the scale bar and the Princeton library stamp. Block 1A is noted at the bottom. 6-inch water pipes are marked in several streets. The header reads Garfield, N.J. and Rutherford; the numbers 37 and 48 are printed at the top and the right edge.
notes: Ely Craft Parkway is modern Elycroft Parkway; Nevins is Nevins Street; Pierrepont Avenue is East Pierrepont Avenue; 8th Avenue was not matched to a modern street.
Nevins is marked not opened.
Barrows Avenue is a modern street not drawn on this sheet; its junction with Summit Avenue was rejected (14 m).
100 ft. Southwest: Summit Av to Meadow Road, Rutherford Av (Union Township line) to Pierrepont Av; mostly open lots. One part.

sheet-48-1.description: The main part of sheet 48 covers the south side of Rutherford between Mountain Way and Meadow Road, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Pierrepont Avenue runs down the left side and the part reaches east past Highland Cross to Sares. Orient Way, Feronia Way and Spring cross the part as long parallel streets, with Summit Cross and Highland Cross running diagonally between them, and Garfield Place, Winslow Place, Elizabeth and Roliver as short cross streets; Ely Craft Parkway begins at Pierrepont Avenue near the lower left. Meadow Road runs along the bottom, and a short Borough Street leads south from it toward the Columbia Button Works, which is drawn in the inset above (part 2). The area is a residential district of detached frame dwellings, densest between Mountain Way and Spring near Summit Cross and Highland Cross, with long narrow lots still largely empty in the large blocks along Pierrepont Avenue and toward Meadow Road. There are no industrial or institutional buildings in this part. Water pipes are marked along most streets, with fire alarm boxes at Pierrepont Avenue and Mountain Way and at Highland Cross. Block numbers 142 to 168 are shown, and sheets 38 and 47 adjoin. A heavy line separates this part from the strip along the Erie Railroad drawn at the bottom of the sheet (part 3).

sheet-48-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 48 is the strip below the heavy line at the bottom of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It continues the south side of Rutherford eastward from East Passaic Avenue to the Erie Railroad and across it into East Rutherford, ending at Union Avenue. Orient Way, Feronia Way and Spring cross the left half, and Meadow Road runs along the bottom. Erie Avenue follows the northwest side of the Erie Railroad's main line, which crosses the strip diagonally with several tracks and a coal trestle; the borough line between Rutherford and East Rutherford is marked along the tracks. Beyond the railroad, Hackensack, Winter Place, Summer (marked not opened), Van Winkle Street and Union Avenue lay out the edge of East Rutherford. The Rutherford side is a district of detached frame dwellings on narrow lots, with Smith's livery, a garage and a store along Erie Avenue. On the East Rutherford side stand the coal yard of the Hassel, Huhn, Williams Co. beside the trestle, a wagon shed, a few dwellings, the Erie Hotel near the station end of Park Avenue, and a large building of the Public Service Railway Co. at the bottom, referred to sheet 45. A base ball field is marked south of Hackensack. Block numbers 77, 97, 98, 99 and 154 to 169 are shown, and sheets 41, 42, 43 and 45 adjoin.
notes: Erie Avenue is modern East Erie Avenue.
Summer is marked not opened.
Hackensack Street and Union Avenue also meet in Hackensack, inside the reference box; the bootstrap point is given by coordinates.
